rv.q: Director Malkia Stampley's production could mitigate those issues if it had higher stakes, much faster pacing and more bite, but the production has slow transitions and, at least at the performance I saw, the actors never really fire up as I think they should and could.
Every artistic choice in the production works together to authentically portray the Black female experience across the 20th and 21st centuries.
Morrisseau’s writing has a keen way of encapsulating the universal experience of Black families.
This play is theatrical magic, an unforgettable experience you need to witness.
Expertly directed by Malkia Stampley, this production is a sublime examination of family, inheritance, and the difficult choices that determine what we pass on to the next generation.
Morisseau’s drama about how a family estrangement poisons and divides its members, until love mends the breach, is a universal story that will touch every audience.
Ultimately, Mud Row is undone by the mechanics and predictability of its script.
Malkia Stampley’s production of Dominique Morisseau’s Mud Row features excellent performances, smart pacing, an evocative set, and even noticeably fine lighting effects (designed by Levi Wilkins).
Folded over an unforgettably probing story about family, excellent acting makes Mud Row a theatrical feast.
Remy Bumppo Theatre Company’s production at Theater Wit, directed by Malkia Stampley, is a compelling production which understands that family history is often never simple.
This is a solid cast of players making each character feel as real as one can be.
If you're looking for a show that shows generational trauma without the tragedy and provides a hopeful outlook of the future, Mud Row would be a great fit for you!

Sadly, themes and questions can only carry you so far, and Dominique Morisseau's multigenerational Mud Row, now being staged at Theater Wit by Remy Bumppo Theatre Company , consistently falters in delivering an experience worth the weight of its ideas.

cn.t: Critics praise the strong performances and direction in this multigenerational family drama about inheritance and legacy, but many find Morisseau's script overstuffed with themes and weighed down by heavy exposition.
